deprecated_yaml.title: Animated Scenes YAML configuration is deprecated
deprecated_yaml.description: Your {integration_title} scenes from YAML ({domain}) are imported automatically into Settings > Devices & Services. A scene is skipped if one with the same name already exists. Once your scenes appear there, remove them from your YAML configuration. Later YAML changes will not update the imported scenes, so edit them in Settings > Devices & Services.

data_description.priority: If multiple animations use the same light, the one with the higher priority will 'win' and take control of the light. Any whole number from -1,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000.
data_description.transition: How many seconds a light should take to transition from its former state to its new state. Can be a number or a range in the format of '[2, 5]' (means to transition the lights over 2 to 5 seconds). Min: 0, Max: 6553.
data_description.change_frequency: After how many seconds the animation should change. Can be a number or a range in the format of '[2, 5]' (means to change lights every 2 to 5 seconds). Use 0 to change the lights once and then stop. Otherwise, Min: 0.1, Max: 3600.
data_description.change_amount: How many lights should be changed each time the frequency is hit. Can be a number, a range in the format of '[2, 5]' (means to change between 2 to 5 lights), or specifying the word 'all' will change all lights each time. Min: 0, Max: 65535.
data_description.ignore_off: When on, lights in the animation list are included even if they are off, and the animation turns them on. When off, lights that are off when the animation starts are skipped.
data_description.restore: When the animation ends, restore lights to their prior state.
data_description.restore_power: When the animation ends, turn any lights that were off back to off.
data_description.change_sequence: If set to true, then color changes will happen in the order they are listed below. If false, colors will be chosen randomly from the list.
data_description.brightness: Brightness used when Animate Brightness is off. Use a single number from 0 to 255; a range such as '[125, 255]' is ignored in that mode. When Animate Brightness is on, each color uses its own brightness instead (255 unless the color sets one).
data_description.animate_brightness: Whether or not to animate the brightness. If false, the scene Brightness (a single number) is sent with every update instead of each color's brightness.
data_description.animate_color: Whether or not to animate the colors. If false, colors will be set once upon startup.
data_description.lights: The lights to include in the animation.

data_description.colors: The list of colors. Due to limitations in Home Assistant, you will need to specify this in YAML form. See [Color Configuration Options]({component_color_config_url}) for details.

color_rgb_ui.title: Animated Scenes

data_description.brightness: Sets the brightness for this color. Can be a number or a range in the format of '[125, 255]' (means to set this color's brightness to somewhere between 125 and 255). Min: 0, Max: 255.
data_description.one_change_per_tick: If set to true, only the brightness OR color will change at one time.
data_description.nearby_colors: If set to a number between 1 and 10, we won't pick this color but will instead pick a 'nearby' color. This is useful for selecting, for example, a red and getting a series of lights of various shades of red. The number represents how 'far' from the original we might pick a color. Set to 0 to disable.
data_description.weight: The higher the number, the more likely a color is to appear in the animation. Min: 0, Max: 255. In random color mode the total weight of all colors must be above 0; sequence mode allows 0.

color_rgb_ui.description:
Select a color to use in the animation.

**Color #{color_count}**
